newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goldfields' Henty gold mine seen low cost.
newsitem.headline: Goldfields' Henty gold mine seen low cost.

text.p: Goldfields Ltd's Henty gold mine in Tasmania may rank as Australia's lowest cash cost gold mining operation, Bell Securities Ltd said on Monday.

The Henty mine could produce between 24,000 and 30,000 ounces by the close of the quarter ending June 30 at an average pre-royalty cost of A$135 to A$160 an ounce, Bell analyst Keith Goode said in a report.
Goldfields pays a 10 percent royalty on gold mined at Henty to Canada-based Euro-Nevada Mining Corp Ltd under an agreement with the previous owner, Little River Goldfields NL.
Cash costs refer to most expenses associated with mining, excluding depreciation an amortisation. "It's usually classified as gold going out the mine's gate," Goode said.
Gold currently fetches about A$445 an ounce.
The cost estimate is based on treatment of 29,000 tonnes of ore grading between 27 and 35 grammes of gold per tonne and possible unit costs of around A$140 a tonne, Goode said.
Despite low cost production at Henty, the mine still must overcome other difficulties, Goode told Reuters.

Bell has changed its stock investment recommendation on Goldfields from hold to hold/sell, based on the prospects for Henty, Goode said. "The Henty orebody is significantly smaller than it was supposed to be," Goode said.
Goode said that while the orebody was initially projected to last for around 4-1/2 years, actual life may only be half that. "That has quite a severe impact on Goldfields," Goode said.

Goldfields took control of the Henty project in 1995 after Goldfields floated on the Australian Stock Exchange as a "pure gold" float. The company incorporated the gold property assets of its parent RGC Ltd and Pancontinental Mining Ltd.
Goldfields shares were unchanged at A$2.10 at midday.

In the March quarter, the Granny Smith mine in Western Australia recorded the lowest average cash cost of A$202.00 an ounce. Granny Smith is owned 60 percent by Placer Dome Inc and 40 percent Delta Gold NL.
On a world scale, the Ity and Ariab gold mines in Africa operated by Adelaide-based Normandy Mining Ltd boast the world's lowest cash costs of A$134 and A$145 an ounce respectively, Goode said.
